logo_override.validation_detail: png, probed via webfetch -> 'Image fetched successfully' (HTTP 200 + image content type); official FNR lockup - white 'FNR' monogram over 'Luxembourg National Research Fund' in fluo green, on the brand's solid steel-blue field
logo_override._award: AFdoc - Aides a la formation doctorale (PhD funding, Luxembourg National Research Fund)

notes: Awarding body is the Luxembourg National Research Fund (FNR), so the FNR mark is correct. Route: the stored official_source_url /funding-instruments/afdoc fetched fine, but its only images are the AFdoc programme promo art (og:image AFdoc_FNR_web_news_funds.jpg - programme artwork, not the body's logo) and four partner marks in the footer (ESCEM, Science Europe, Research Luxembourg), all third parties. The real header and footer FNR logos on fnr.lu are INLINE <svg> elements (class 'header-brand', and a viewBox='0 0 198.43 32.46' footer mark) with no src, so they cannot be probed or hot-linked. The site's own brand page https://www.fnr.lu/logo/ ('FNR Logo & Communication Guidelines', linked from its own News/Media menu) is the correct place per the brief's step 3, but its hero/logo artwork is only offered as GIFs (fnr-logo-gif-2023-blue-white.gif and fnr-logo-gif_2023-blue-white-v2.gif, both probed 200) - GIF is not an accepted image_format and the white-on-blue treatment is aimed at a dark hero. Its 'Download FNR Logo' button points at a SharePoint folder (fnrlu.sharepoint.com), i.e. a third party. What that same brand page does publish on fnr.lu is the FNR's own brand asset as a PNG: cropped-FNR_ProfilePic_linkedin-32x32/180x180/192x192/270x270.png (referenced as the site's favicon, apple-touch-icon and msapplication-TileImage) - these are the FNR brand lockup, not a personal photo. I probed the 192x192 and 270x270 crops (both 200 + image) and then the uncropped original at the same wp-content path, which returned the highest-resolution copy and is what I recorded. Rule 3 checked: the white monogram sits on an OPAQUE steel-blue square, not on transparency, so it stays fully visible on a light card.
